name: AR-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district (R+13 PVI) with incumbent Steve Womack running
Womack's large financial edge ($2.4M on hand vs. ~$6K for Ryerse)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 6%
No polling or expert ratings available, adding uncertainty
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Womack: a Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising advantage, with markets agreeing at roughly 5% for Democrats. With no polls or ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays close to the baseline.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Ryerse within single digits, or a surge in Democratic outside spending, would be the first sign this is more than a safe Republican hold.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Arkansas's third district is solidly Republican territory, and Steve Womack is seeking another term with the advantages of incumbency and a well-funded campaign. He has raised about $1.9 million and holds $2.4 million on hand, while Democrat Robb Ryerse has raised roughly $120,000 with little left to spend. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Ryerse only about a 6% chance. Womack is the clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for surprise.
